title: Officer told of 'suicide by cop,' inquest hears
article: A man armed with a knife talked with officers about suicide minutes before police shot him, an officer testified at an inquest Monday.
The week-long hearing into the 2005 death of Howard Fleury began Monday.
Fleury, 34, died at a home at 339 Alfred Ave. on Dec. 2 after police shot him repeatedly.

A lawyer for police told the media soon after Fleury's death the distraught man mentioned "suicide by cop" after officers responded there for a domestic dispute. The term came up again at the hearing Monday. Const. Randall Dziver said when he arrived at the home, other officers on scene told him Fleury referred to "suicide by cop" while arguing with police near the back door of the home.
"He (Fleury) said, 'Have you ever heard of suicide by cop?'" said Dziver, who said he was guarding outside the front of 339 Alfred when police shot Fleury.

Fleury's estranged common-law wife, Kimberly Desjarlais, lived at the property and had called police after Fleury arrived intoxicated. Desjarlais told Judge Catherine Carlson Monday she instructed her daughter to bundle all the kitchen knives and hide them from her father after he arrived at the home. Desjarlais later called police for help.
After officers arrived, Desjarlais and some of her children waited in the basement of the home as officers yelled at Fleury on the main floor of the home.
Desjarlais said Monday that, because a door was closed, she could not understand what Fleury said to police in response.
Police later shot Fleury in the home after an attempt to pepper-spray the distraught six-foot-tall man failed, court heard.
After he heard a series of what sounded like four gunshots, Dziver said, he saw two police officers he knew exit the home looking "drained."
"Their heads were down. Their shoulders were sagged," he said.
Police had to carry two small children who had been upstairs out over the corpse.

A thick knife with a wooden handle was entered as an exhibit at the inquest hearing Monday. Another detailed diagram showed the layout of 339 Alfred, where Fleury spent his final minutes, including eight knife punctures on the staircase wall.
Desjarlais said she was not aware until informed later that Fleury had cocaine in his blood system when he died.
However, she said, he was drinking liquor at the home before she called police.
Some of Fleury's eight children with Desjarlais were at the hearing.
